_comment: compute/virtualserver — VS 4-action VERIFY recipe (HEAVY-PREMISE-CONTRACT WP4, 2026-07-08). One HEAVY lifecycle that creates a minimal throwaway server and earns real 2xx on the 4 safe per-server write actions the validated compute-virtualserver-full spine deliberately omits: password / dump / server-type(resize) / rebuild. Conventions (create-server body, captures, ready polls, teardown order) copied from compute-virtualserver-full (scenarios.json, READ-ONLY reference) and gen-heavy-vs-netops. lock/unlock are deliberately ABSENT: stranding risk, owner-waived class:reachability 2026-07-08 (data/baselines/coverage_waivers.json) — the CI-lane probe vs-server-action-coverage keeps them REACHED.

lifecycles._note: Composed for ENDPOINT-DEPTH: earns real 2xx on the 4 safe server actions the heavy full lifecycle omits — POST password, POST dump, POST server-type (resize), POST rebuild — then tears everything down. Runs ONLY under the heavy opt-in (billable VM ~17min class). Steps expect strict 2xx so the loader derives role=verify (contract §1); the one documented exception is password [200,400] = PF-17 (Linux servers have no encrypted admin password to decrypt — live 400 VirtualServer.InvalidPrivateKeyValue, run 27452095757; a real 2xx needs a Windows image, out of minimal-throwaway scope). Do NOT enable lock/unlock here (risk of stranding a billable VM undeletable — same deadlock class as the 2 stranded SCF functions in known_issues; owner-waived class:reachability 2026-07-08, exercised by the CI probe vs-server-action-coverage instead). Action order per plan: password -> dump (both on ACTIVE) -> stop -> server-type resize (SCP type change needs a STOPPED server; api_docs is silent on state, conservative) -> start -> rebuild (on ACTIVE, the standard path; docs list no request body — rebuilds from the server's own image) -> delete. create uses the fixed smallest standard type s1v1m2 (docs example; live-accepted by the ASG launch-configuration create 2026-06-19) so the resize target — first catalog s-type that is not s1v1m2 and not a g/GPU type, captured BEFORE the billable create so a missing type fails fast — is a valid different/larger type (standard ladder: s1v2m4-class).

steps.name: create-vpc
steps._note: Adopts the session-shared VPC when SCP_SHARED_VPC_ID is set (engine seeds vpc_id, skips this create); self-create fallback CIDR 10.176.0.0/20 is a unique range (no overlap with any other fragment or the shared 10.124.0.0/20).

steps.name: create-keypair
steps._note: STRICT 2xx (no 409 orphan tolerance like the full lifecycle): the password action needs THIS keypair's private_key from the create response ($.private_key, KeypairCreateResponse top-level — formal model VALIDATED); an orphan reuse would leave it uncapturable.

steps.name: find-resize-server-type
steps._note: Resize target: first standard s-type that is NOT the create type s1v1m2 and NOT a g/GPU type. s1v1m2 is the smallest standard size (v1m2 = 1 vCPU/2GB, ladder floor per docs + billingplan css ladder), so any other s-type is a valid larger/different type (expected s1v2m4-class). HARD capture placed BEFORE the billable create-server on purpose: an account with no second s-type fails fast here instead of churning a VM.

steps.name: create-server
steps._note: Body verbatim from the VALIDATED compute-virtualserver-full create (array capture envelope $.servers[0].id, boot volume type SSD size 104 delete_on_termination true) EXCEPT server_type_id is pinned to the smallest standard s1v1m2 so the resize target is deterministically different (the full lifecycle's dynamic first-s-type capture would make 'different from current' inexpressible).

steps.name: get-server-password
steps._note: showvirtualserverpassword with the REAL keypair private_key (read-only effect). [200,400] = PF-17: live 400 VirtualServer.InvalidPrivateKeyValue 'Failed to decrypt' (run 27452095757) — Linux/ubuntu servers have no encrypted admin password (Windows-only feature); the private_key capture itself is fine. The only non-strict action step; a genuine 2xx needs a Windows image.

steps.name: dump-server
steps._note: createvirtualserverdump — no request body (api_docs: server_id path param only; 202 Accepted). Strict-2xx on an ACTIVE server is live-proven: gen-heavy-vs-netops runs the same step non-optional and its later static-nat steps were proven 2xx in run 27450089575.

steps.name: stop-server
steps._note: Same endpoint/expectation as the full lifecycle's validated stop; 409-retry armor in case the dump is still materializing when stop fires.

steps.name: resize-server-type
steps._note: setvirtualservertype on the STOPPED server (SCP console requires stopped for a type change; api_docs states no server-state precondition, so stopped is the conservative path). Body field is server_type per the docs model serversetservertyperequestbody — NOT server_type_id (the old coverage probe's unproven guess).

steps.name: wait-server-resized
steps._note: Resize is async (202); the server returns to STOPPED when it completes. The 15s pre-sleep lets the state leave STOPPED for its transitional value first, defeating the instant-pass race; start-server below carries 409-retry armor for any residue.

steps.name: rebuild-server
steps._note: rebuildvirtualserver — api_docs lists NO request body (server_id path param only): reinstalls the OS from the server's own image, so nothing external is wiped in. Run on ACTIVE (the standard rebuild path); 409-retry armor if the resize/start is still settling. Ordered last of the 4 actions since it re-provisions the guest.

steps.name: wait-server-rebuilt
steps._note: 20s pre-sleep lets the state flip out of ACTIVE into the rebuild transition before polling back to ACTIVE; if the platform never surfaces a transition this passes immediately and delete-server's 409-retry absorbs a still-rebuilding delete.
